title: reading a Result's runtime discriminant is not one of the five acts that discharge the must-use rule
notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Matching and Transformation': 'A Result MUST be treated as a must-use value. A source program MUST NOT silently discard a Result without returning, matching, transforming, inspecting, or unwrapping it.' The sentence that settles whether a `.ok` read is the 'inspecting' act is one section earlier, in 'Compiler-Owned Modules': `smthrs/result` 'is the lowering target: emitted code imports it... The compiler links it directly, `!` and `expect` are rejected inside it, and its public API is instance methods.' `ok` is a property of the lowering target's runtime classes, not an instance method — and the page's own inspection group is `isOk isError match`, three methods and no properties, of which 07-must-consume/every-listed-consumption-form-is-accepted already pins `isError()` as the inspecting form. WHAT THE CASE PINS is the binding's SMITHERS1302: `outcome` is read three times and consumed by none of them. THIS WAS A FORK FAIL-OPEN AND IS NOW FIXED. Landed 2026-08-28 as an `xfail(go)` marker and retired in the same lane after an XPASS: the fork accepted, compiled and RAN this program (exit 0, printing `zoe` — it extracted the ERROR value and read a field off it with no `!`, no `match`, no `unwrapOr` and no `expect`). The cause was one arm in `compiler/forkbridge/mustconsume.go.txt`: inside `boundConsumeResult`, a bare member SELECTION whose symbol resolved to one of the four declarations `collectResultInspectionMembers` indexes (`ok` on each of `SmithersOk`/`SmithersErr`, plus the `value`/`error` readonly constructor parameters) returned `true` before the walk ever asked whether the member was CALLED. Removing that arm makes every discharge require a call, which is what the reference has always required. The three-line predicate it fed (`preludeSymbols.resultInspection`) is deleted; the four declarations are still collected, because the prelude completeness check counts them as a shape assertion. VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, one variable at a time, on both backends. (1) The recognized spelling still discharges — `return outcome.isError()` compiles clean on both — so the rule refuses the PROPERTY read, not inspection as such; `compiler/fork_mustconsume_test.go` now asserts both halves, and its first subtest is the INVERSION of one that had asserted the fail-open under the name 'compiler-owned Result inspection consumes the binding'. (2) `outcome.value` and `outcome.error` read WITHOUT a `.ok` guard were already `TS2339` on BOTH backends, so the discriminant was the only gateway. (3) `isOk()` narrows on NEITHER backend (`if (outcome.isOk()) { return [outcome.value] }` is `TS2339` at `.value` on both), which is why the fork's `.ok` had become the only narrowing spelling either implementation had, and why this read as a capability rather than a slip. (4) THE LABEL WAS A RED HERRING. The defect arrived reported as `outer: { … break outer; … }`. 41 labeled-form probes were measured — labeled blocks, non-block labeled statements, labeled `while`/`do`/`for`/`for-of`/`switch`, bare and labeled `break`/`continue`, nested and duplicate labels, and labels inside arrows, nested functions and object methods — and the two backends agree on every one; wrapping this program in a labeled block changes neither backend's answer. It is NOT a member of the `statementMayFallThrough` class that 02-unwrap-propagation/postfix-bang-in-a-labeled-statement-body-is-accepted records. WHAT IS NOT CLOSED, stated so the next reader does not assume it is: `outcome.ok` still TYPECHECKS on the fork. With the obligation discharged another way first (`const name = outcome.unwrapOr(-1)` above the tag read) the fork compiles and runs the read while the reference reports `TS2339`, because the fork's authored `Result` IS the union of its two runtime classes while the reference's is an opaque interface of fifteen instance methods (`RESULT_MEMBER_SIGNATURES`). Separating them needs the fork to grow an authored-facing Result declaration distinct from the representation its own lowering emits `.ok` reads against, which is a design change rather than a walk fix. That residual is fail-CLOSED on the reference and accepts nothing this case forbids. Related and also open: failures.mdx 'Authorability' marks 'Whether Smithers gains an error-extraction form' Open, so if the ledger owner adds one, this case is the thing to re-read — the must-use consequence is what is locked, the spelling is not.
